groups.title: Tablet (D33500ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for neuralgia, back pain and stiff shoulders.
groups.usage: Adults: take 1 to 2 tablets per dose, 2 times in 1 day, when pain or an attack occurs.
groups.caution:
Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have hypersensitivity to medicines; if you have a constitution prone to urticaria, contact dermatitis, bronchial asthma, allergic rhinitis, migraine or food allergy; if you have had allergic symptoms (for example fever, rash, joint pain, asthma or itching); if the user is a baby, a young child or a child (aged 14 years or younger) with, or suspected of having, chickenpox or influenza; if you have liver, kidney or thyroid disease, diabetes or high blood pressure; if you have a high fever or are physically weak; if you are an older person; or if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. When it is given to a child, use it under the supervision of a guardian.

Do not take it together with another antipyretic analgesic, a cold medicine or a sedative.

If rash, reddening of the skin, nausea, vomiting, constipation, loss of appetite or vertigo occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

summaryTable.What it is for: Neuralgia, back pain and stiff shoulders

groups.title: Tablet (E61700ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the supply of vitamins D, B1, B2 and B6 in physical tiredness, during pregnancy and breast-feeding, when strength is reduced during or after illness, during growth and in old age. Through the vitamins it contains, this medicine is used for the relief of neuralgia, muscle pain, back pain, joint pain such as stiff shoulders, angular cheilitis, cheilitis, stomatitis, glossitis, eczema and dermatitis. Through the vitamins it contains, this medicine is used for poor development of the bones and teeth, for the prevention of rickets, and for beriberi and eye strain.
groups.usage: Adults aged 19 years and older: take 1 tablet per dose, 1 time in 1 day.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if the user is a baby under 12 months of age; or if you have high blood calcium, sarcoidosis, kidney disease or kidney stones.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; if the user is a premature baby or a young child; if you have impaired heart or circulatory function or kidney impairment; if you have hypoproteinaemia; or if you have had kidney stones.

If symptoms do not improve after taking it for 1 month or more, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist. If you are short of folic acid, consult a pharmacist. It may turn the urine yellow and so affect clinical test values. Keep to the stated dosage and schedule.

While you are taking this medicine, do not take a phosphate, a calcium salt, an oral tetracycline preparation, an antacid or levodopa. Consult a pharmacist if you take it together with an antialdosterone medicine or triamterene. Avoid tannin-containing drinks such as green tea and black tea while taking it and just before and after taking it.

If nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, loose stools, constipation, loss of appetite, erythema, urticaria, eczema, rash, maculopapular rash, itching, oedema, or fluid retention in people with kidney failure or heart failure occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

summaryTable.What it is for: Supply of vitamins D, B1, B2 and B6, relief of neuralgia, muscle and joint pain, cheilitis, stomatitis, glossitis, eczema and dermatitis, poor bone and tooth development, prevention of rickets, beriberi and eye strain

summaryTable.Ask the pharmacist: Ask the pharmacist in the store first if any of the cautions above apply to you.

groups.title: Soft Capsule (142301ACS)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for chronic polyarthritis, rheumatoid arthritis, arthrosis, ankylosing spondylitis, painful swelling or inflammation after injury and surgery, and as an aid in the treatment of infections accompanied by inflammation, pain and fever.
groups.usage: Adults: take 1 capsule (300 mg) per dose, 2 to 4 times in 1 day. Do not exceed 4 capsules (1200 mg) in 1 day.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day, consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause gastrointestinal bleeding.

Taking this medicine increases the risk of serious and possibly fatal cardiovascular thrombotic events, myocardial infarction and stroke, and serious gastrointestinal adverse reactions such as gastrointestinal bleeding, ulceration and perforation may occur.

People with uncontrolled high blood pressure, congestive heart failure, established ischaemic heart disease, peripheral arterial disease or cerebrovascular disease must avoid high-dose dexibuprofen (1,200 mg a day); people with cardiovascular risk factors (high blood pressure, high blood lipids, diabetes, smoking and the like) who need high-dose dexibuprofen (1,200 mg a day) must consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if you have or have had gastrointestinal ulcer; if you have bleeding in the gastrointestinal tract, the cerebral blood vessels or elsewhere; if you have a severe blood disorder, severe liver impairment, severe kidney impairment, severe cardiac insufficiency or severe high blood pressure; if you have or have had bronchial asthma; if you have had asthma, urticaria or an allergic reaction to aspirin or another non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesic; if it is for the treatment of pain before or after coronary artery bypass graft surgery (CABG); if you are 6 months or more pregnant; if you are breast-feeding; if you have inflammatory bowel disease such as Crohn's disease or ulcerative colitis; or if you have had gastrointestinal bleeding or perforation during earlier treatment with a non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesic.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have or have had a blood disorder; if you have a tendency to bleed; if you have or have had liver impairment or kidney impairment; if you have fluid retention or heart failure; if you have high blood pressure; if you have had hypersensitivity; if you have systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) or mixed connective tissue disease (MCTD); if you are an older person; if the user is a child aged 6 years or older; if you have stomach cancer or alcoholism; if you are in early or mid pregnancy or may be pregnant; if you have ischaemic heart disease, peripheral arterial disease, cerebrovascular disease or risk factors for cardiovascular disease (for example high blood pressure, high blood lipids, diabetes, smoking); if you have hepatic porphyria; if you have had major surgery with blood loss; if you have a blood clotting disorder or are being given an anticoagulant; or if you have or have had hypersensitivity to Yellow No. 5 (Sunset Yellow FCF).

Considering the importance of the treatment, either stop breast-feeding or stop taking the medicine. Dizziness or fatigue may occur after taking it, so take care when driving or operating machinery. When it is taken for a long period for an acute illness, as a rule this should be within 5 days.

Do not take it together with aspirin, another non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesic or high-dose methotrexate (15 mg a week or more) used as cancer treatment. Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you take it together with a corticosteroid, alcohol, digoxin, phenytoin, probenecid, sulfinpyrazone, a sulfonylurea, an ACE inhibitor, an angiotensin II receptor antagonist, a diuretic, lithium, a coumarin anticoagulant (warfarin and the like), baclofen, an immunosuppressant (ciclosporin, tacrolimus, sirolimus), a thrombolytic, ticlopidine, an antithrombotic, a medicine that raises blood potassium (trimethoprim, heparin and the like), an inducer of CYP2C8 or CYP2C9 (for example rifampicin or phenobarbital), low-dose methotrexate (less than 15 mg a week), an antiplatelet medicine or a selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor, or if you take low-dose aspirin to prevent myocardial infarction or stroke.

If any of the following occur, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist: rarely shock (chest discomfort, chills, difficulty breathing, a fall in blood pressure and the like); rarely blood disorders such as aplastic anaemia, haemolytic anaemia, granulocytopenia, leukopenia, agranulocytosis, pancytopenia, thrombocytopenia, reduced platelet function (prolonged bleeding time) or eosinophilia; indigestion, abdominal distension, heartburn, upper abdominal pain, diarrhoea or constipation; occasionally loss of appetite, nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain or stomach discomfort; rarely oesophagitis, oesophageal stricture, worsening of diverticula, non-specific haemorrhagic colitis, ulcerative colitis or Crohn's disease, peptic ulcer, gastrointestinal bleeding, perforation, bloody stools, gastritis or pancreatitis; very rarely thirst, stomatitis, erythema multiforme, systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) or hair loss; occasionally angioedema; rarely Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome); drug rash with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS syndrome) of unknown frequency; acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis; occasionally rash, urticaria, itching or purpura; rarely triggering of an asthma attack, eczema, an anaphylactic reaction or a photosensitivity reaction; rarely jaundice, raised ALT, raised AST, raised ALP, abnormal liver function or hepatitis; occasionally rhinitis, bronchospasm or acute pneumonia; rarely visual disturbance such as scotoma or dark spots, hearing loss, tinnitus or taste disturbance; fatigue, drowsiness, headache or dizziness; occasionally anxiety, restlessness, confusion or depression; rarely aseptic meningitis, severe headache, nausea, vomiting, insomnia, a stiff neck, fever or disturbance of consciousness; rarely mental disturbance, agitation, excitement, disorientation or reversible toxic amblyopia; rarely a fall or rise in blood pressure, palpitations, reduced urine output, blood in the urine, protein in the urine, raised BUN or blood creatinine, high blood potassium, reduced urine volume, generalised oedema with breathlessness or lassitude; rarely renal papillary necrosis, nephrotic syndrome, interstitial nephritis, peripheral oedema, acute pulmonary oedema, fluid retention, high blood pressure, heart failure or reduced fertility in women; occasionally swelling around the eye sockets; very rarely malaise, fever, nosebleed or worsening of inflammation.

groups.title: Tablet (E73100ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the supply of vitamins D, B1, B2 and B6 in physical tiredness, during pregnancy and breast-feeding, when strength is reduced during or after illness, during growth and in old age, for poor development of the bones and teeth, for the prevention of rickets, for the relief of beriberi, eye strain, neuralgia, muscle pain, joint pain (back pain, stiff shoulders and the like), angular cheilitis, cheilitis, stomatitis, glossitis, eczema and dermatitis, and for the supply of zinc.
groups.usage: Adults and those aged 12 years and older: take 1 tablet per dose, 1 time in 1 day, after a meal.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if the user is a baby under 12 months of age; if you have high blood calcium, sarcoidosis, kidney disease, kidney stones or severe renal failure; if you have or have had hypersensitivity or an allergic reaction to soybean oil; or if you have hypersensitivity to soybean or peanut.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; if the user is a premature baby or a young child; if the user is a baby under 1 year of age; if the user is a child who gets plenty of sunlight and eats a normal diet; if you have a gastrointestinal disease such as peptic ulcer, chronic ulcerative colitis or regional enteritis; if you have impaired heart or circulatory function, kidney impairment or hypoproteinaemia; if you have had kidney stones; or if you have a disorder of fat metabolism such as hyperlipoproteinaemia, diabetic hyperlipidaemia or pancreatitis, or lipid emulsions must be given to you with caution.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. It may turn the urine yellow and so affect clinical test values. When it is given to a child, use it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.

Do not take it together with a phosphate, a calcium salt, an oral tetracycline preparation, an antacid or levodopa. Consult a pharmacist if you take it together with an oral contraceptive containing oestrogen. Taking it together with an antialdosterone medicine or triamterene may cause high blood potassium, so take care. Avoid tannin-containing drinks such as green tea and black tea while taking it and just before and after taking it.

If nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, loose stools, red spots, cardiac arrest, reduced central nervous system function, dermatitis, a bad smell in the sweat or breath, hair loss, irritability, gastrointestinal disturbance, digestive disturbance, upper abdominal pain, low blood pressure or pulmonary oedema occurs, or if symptoms do not improve after about 1 month of use, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.title: Capsule (268600ACH)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for cough and phlegm.
groups.usage: Adults: take 2 capsules per dose, 3 times in 1 day, after meals.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have or have had hypersensitivity to it; if you are pregnant or may be pregnant; or if the user is a baby under 3 months of age or a child under 2 years of age.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have or have had hypersensitivity to Yellow No. 5; if the user is a child under 2 years of age for whom it is really necessary; if you have an allergic constitution or have had allergic symptoms caused by a medicine (for example fever, rash, joint pain or itching); if you have liver, kidney, heart or thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, glaucoma (for example eye pain or blurred vision) or difficulty passing urine; if you are an older person, physically weak or have a high fever; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; or if you smoke or have asthma, chronic bronchitis, emphysema, a cough with excessive sputum, a cough lasting or recurring for 1 week or more, a chronic cough, or a cough with fever, rash or persistent headache.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. If symptoms do not improve after 5 to 6 doses, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist. Drowsiness may occur after taking it, so take care when driving or operating machinery.

Do not take it together with an MAO inhibitor (antidepressant, antipsychotic, mood stabiliser, anti-Parkinson medicine and the like), another antitussive-expectorant, a cold medicine, an oral medicine containing an antihistamine (oral medicine for rhinitis, motion-sickness medicine, anti-allergy medicine) or a sedative. Do not take this medicine if you have stopped taking an MAO inhibitor (antidepressant, antipsychotic, mood stabiliser, anti-Parkinson medicine and the like) within the past 2 weeks.

If rash and reddening of the skin, itching, nausea and vomiting, loss of appetite, dizziness, difficulty passing urine, persistent or severe thirst, anxiety, tremor or insomnia occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.title: Tablet (A06600ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for loss of appetite, abdominal distension, abnormal fermentation in the intestine and haemorrhoids.
groups.usage: Adults and those aged 15 years and older: take 1 tablet per dose, 3 times in 1 day, before meals (between meals or after meals). Ages 11 years to under 15 years: take 1 tablet per dose, 2 times in 1 day, in the morning and in the evening on an empty stomach. Leave an interval of at least 4 hours between doses. For the first dose take the smallest amount, then increase or decrease it gradually while watching the form and condition of the stool.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have an acute abdominal disease (appendicitis, intestinal bleeding, ulcerative colitis and the like) or intestinal obstruction (blocked bowel), or if the user is a child aged 7 years or younger.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have severe abdominal pain, nausea or vomiting; if you are pregnant or may be pregnant; if you have kidney impairment; or if you have had rectal bleeding or intestinal failure.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. When it is given to a child, use it under the supervision of a guardian.

Do not take it together with an antacid. Avoid taking it within 1 hour after drinking milk.

If rash and reddening of the skin, itching, severe abdominal pain, diarrhoea, vomiting, abdominal discomfort or cramps occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.title: Enteric-coated Tablet (308000ATE)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the relief of inflammatory swelling after surgery and injury and in milk stasis.
groups.usage: Adults: on the first day take 2 tablets per dose, 4 times in 1 day; after that, as a maintenance dose, take 1 tablet per dose, 4 times in 1 day. Much about how it works in the body is still not explained and the relationship between dose and effect has not been established, so do not take it without a clear purpose.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you are pregnant or may be pregnant; if you have a blood clotting disorder; if you have severe liver impairment or kidney impairment; or if you have or have had hypersensitivity to Yellow No. 4.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule.

Consult a pharmacist if you take it together with an anticoagulant.

If rash, reddening of the skin, diarrhoea or constipation occurs, or occasionally loss of appetite, abdominal discomfort, nausea or vomiting, or rarely a tendency to bleed such as nosebleed or blood in the sputum occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for diarrhoea, diarrhoea with abdominal pain, indigestion, loose stools and vomiting with diarrhoea.
groups.usage: Adults and those aged 15 years and older: take 2 tablets per dose, 3 times in 1 day, after meals, leaving an interval of at least 4 hours.

Do not take this medicine if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; if the user is a newborn baby or a child aged 7 years or younger; or if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have had allergic symptoms caused by a medicine; if you have diarrhoea with fever; if you are an older person; if you have bloody stools or continuing mucous stools; if you have gastric or duodenal ulcer; or if you have had hypersensitivity or an allergic reaction to Yellow No. 4.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. Do not keep taking it for 3 days or more.

Do not take it together with a gastrointestinal analgesic or antispasmodic. Do not drink alcohol while taking it.

If allergic symptoms (rash, itching and the like) or, rarely, dry mouth occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.title: Tablet (D12500ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the relief of the various symptoms of a cold (sore throat, cough, phlegm, chills with shivering, fever, headache, joint pain, muscle pain).
groups.usage: Adults: take 1 tablet per dose, 3 times in 1 day, 30 minutes after meals.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day, consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause liver damage.

Very rarely, serious skin reactions that may be fatal, such as acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis, have been reported. If a skin rash or any other sign of hypersensitivity appears after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.

Do not exceed the maximum daily dose of acetaminophen (4,000 mg). It may cause liver damage. Do not take it together with other products that contain acetaminophen.

Do not take this medicine if you have or have had hypersensitivity to it; if you have had asthma after taking another antipyretic analgesic or a cold medicine; if the user is a child under 2 years of age; or if you are taking an MAO inhibitor (antidepressant, antipsychotic, mood stabiliser, anti-Parkinson medicine and the like) or have stopped taking one within the past 2 weeks.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if the user is a baby or a child under 15 years of age with, or suspected of having, chickenpox or influenza; if you have an allergic constitution or have had allergic symptoms caused by a medicine (for example fever, rash, joint pain, asthma or itching); if you have liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure or gastric or duodenal ulcer; if you are an older person, physically weak or have a high fever; if you have persistent or recurring stomach problems such as heartburn, stomach discomfort or stomach pain, or an ulcer or bleeding problem; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; or if you have had hypersensitivity or an allergic reaction to Yellow No. 4.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. If symptoms do not improve after 5 to 6 doses, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

Do not take it together with an antitussive-expectorant, another cold medicine, an antipyretic analgesic, a sedative, or an oral medicine containing an antihistamine (oral medicine for rhinitis, motion-sickness medicine, anti-allergy medicine). Consult a pharmacist if you take it together with barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants, alcohol, a diabetes medicine, a gout medicine, an arthritis medicine, an anticoagulant or a steroid. Do not drink alcohol while taking it.

If rash and reddening of the skin, itching, nausea and vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, swelling, dizziness, anxiety, tremor or insomnia occurs, or if, rarely, signs of shock (urticaria, swelling and chest tightness soon after taking it, together with pallor, cold hands and feet, cold sweat and difficulty breathing), Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome, with high fever, rash and reddening of the skin and severe burn-like blisters), asthma, general lassitude, jaundice (yellowing of the skin or the whites of the eyes) or interstitial pneumonia (cough, breathlessness, difficulty breathing, fever) occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

If symptoms of posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome or reversible cerebral vasoconstriction syndrome (sudden severe headache, thunderclap headache, nausea, vomiting, confusion, seizure, visual disturbance and the like) occur, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; if the user is a premature baby or a young child; if you have impaired heart or circulatory function, kidney impairment or hypoproteinaemia; if you have had kidney stones; if you have a disorder of fat metabolism such as hyperlipoproteinaemia, diabetic hyperlipidaemia or pancreatitis, or lipid emulsions must be given to you with caution; or if you have fat overload.

If symptoms do not improve after about 1 month of use, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist. If you are short of folic acid, consult a pharmacist. It may turn the urine yellow and so affect clinical test values. Keep to the stated dosage and schedule.

While you are taking this medicine, do not take a phosphate, a calcium salt, an oral tetracycline preparation, an antacid or levodopa. Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you are being given a cardiac glycoside. Consult a pharmacist if you take it together with an antialdosterone medicine or triamterene. Avoid tannin-containing drinks such as green tea and black tea while taking it and just before and after taking it.

If nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, loose stools, constipation, low blood pressure, facial flushing, an irregular heartbeat, skin rash, red spots, cardiac arrest, reduced central nervous system function, loss of appetite, erythema, eczema, rash, maculopapular rash, itching, oedema, or fluid retention in people with heart failure occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.title: Soft Capsule (D22300ACS)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the relief of the various symptoms of a cold (runny nose, blocked nose, sneezing, sore throat, cough, phlegm, chills with shivering, fever, headache, joint pain, muscle pain).
groups.usage: Adults and those aged 15 years and older: take 2 capsules per dose. Ages 7 years to under 15 years: take 1 capsule per dose. Take it 3 times in 1 day, 30 minutes after meals.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day, consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause liver damage.

Very rarely, serious skin reactions that may be fatal, such as acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis, have been reported. If a skin rash or any other sign of hypersensitivity appears after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.

Do not exceed the maximum daily dose of acetaminophen (4,000 mg). It may cause liver damage. Do not take it together with other products that contain acetaminophen.

Do not take this medicine if you have or have had hypersensitivity to it; if you have had asthma after taking another antipyretic analgesic or a cold medicine; if the user is a baby under 3 months of age; or if you are taking an MAO inhibitor (antidepressant, antipsychotic, mood stabiliser, anti-Parkinson medicine and the like) or have stopped taking one within the past 2 weeks.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if the user is a baby or a child under 15 years of age with, or suspected of having, chickenpox or influenza; if the user is a baby or young child aged 3 months or older and under 2 years of age; if you have an allergic constitution or have had allergic symptoms (for example fever, rash, joint pain, asthma or itching); if you have liver, kidney, heart or thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, gastric or duodenal ulcer, glaucoma (for example eye pain or blurred vision) or difficulty passing urine; if you are physically weak or have a high fever; if you have persistent or recurring stomach problems such as heartburn, stomach discomfort or stomach pain, or an ulcer or bleeding problem; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; or if you smoke or have asthma, chronic bronchitis, emphysema, a cough with excessive sputum, a cough lasting or recurring for 1 week or more, a chronic cough, or a cough with fever, rash or persistent headache.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. Do not drink alcohol while taking it. Drowsiness may occur after taking it, so take care when driving or operating machinery. Do not take it continuously for a long period. When it is given to a child, use it under the supervision of a guardian. If symptoms do not improve after about 5 to 6 doses, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

Do not take it together with other products containing acetaminophen, an MAO inhibitor (antidepressant, antipsychotic, mood stabiliser, anti-Parkinson medicine and the like), an antitussive-expectorant, another cold medicine, an antipyretic analgesic, a sedative, or an oral medicine containing an antihistamine (oral medicine for rhinitis, motion-sickness medicine, anti-allergy medicine). Consult a pharmacist if you have been given a diabetes medicine, a gout medicine, an arthritis medicine, an anticoagulant, a steroid, barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants or alcohol.

If rash and reddening of the skin, itching, nausea and vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, oedema, difficulty passing urine, persistent or severe thirst, dizziness, signs of shock (rarely urticaria, swelling and chest tightness after taking it, together with pallor, cold hands and feet, cold sweat and difficulty breathing), Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (with high fever, rash and reddening of the skin and severe burn-like blisters), asthma, general lassitude, jaundice or interstitial pneumonia (cough, breathlessness, difficulty breathing, fever) occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.title: Soft Capsule (E78400ACS)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for constipation and for the relief of the loss of appetite, abdominal distension, abnormal fermentation in the intestine and haemorrhoids that follow constipation.
groups.usage: Adults aged 15 years and older: take 2 capsules per dose, 1 time in 1 day, at bedtime. For the first dose take the smallest amount, then increase or decrease it gradually while watching the form and condition of the stool.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have an acute abdominal disease such as appendicitis, intestinal bleeding or ulcerative colitis; if you have intestinal obstruction; if you have or have had hypersensitivity to soybean oil; or if you have hypersensitivity to soybean or peanut.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if the user is a child aged 10 years or younger; if you are pregnant or may be pregnant; if you have severe abdominal pain, nausea or vomiting; if you are on a sodium-restricted diet; if you have had rectal bleeding or intestinal failure; if you have a disorder of fat metabolism such as hyperlipoproteinaemia, diabetic hyperlipidaemia or pancreatitis, or lipid emulsions must be given to you with caution; if you have fat overload; or if you have or have had hypersensitivity to Yellow No. 5 or Sunset Yellow FCF.

If constipation does not improve after about 1 week of use, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist. Do not keep taking it for 1 week or more. Keep to the stated dosage and schedule.

Do not take this medicine within 1 hour after taking an antacid or drinking milk. (Avoid drinking milk or taking an antacid within 1 hour after taking this medicine.)

If rash, reddening of the skin, itching, severe abdominal pain, diarrhoea, vomiting, abdominal discomfort or cramps occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.title: Tablet (101305ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for fever and pain caused by a cold, headache, neuralgia, muscle pain, menstrual pain, pain from a sprain, toothache, joint pain and rheumatic pain.
groups.usage: Adults: take 300 to 1000 mg per dose, 3 to 4 times in 1 day. Up to 8 tablets (4000 mg) may be given in 1 day. The dose may be increased or decreased appropriately according to age and symptoms.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day, consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause liver damage.

Very rarely, serious skin reactions that may be fatal, such as acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis, have been reported. If a skin rash or any other sign of hypersensitivity appears after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.

Do not exceed the maximum daily dose of acetaminophen (4,000 mg). It may cause liver damage. Do not take it together with other products that contain acetaminophen.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it, peptic ulcer, a severe blood disorder, severe liver impairment, severe kidney impairment or severely reduced heart function; if you have or have had aspirin asthma (an asthma attack triggered by a non-steroidal anti-inflammatory medicine); if you have taken barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants or alcohol; or if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have or have had liver impairment or kidney impairment; if you have had peptic ulcer; if you have or have had a blood disorder; if you have a tendency to bleed; if you have impaired heart function; if you have bronchial asthma; if you are an older person; or if you are pregnant or breast-feeding.

Do not take it together with another anti-inflammatory analgesic, other products containing acetaminophen, barbiturates or tricyclic antidepressants. Consult a pharmacist if you take it together with warfarin, lithium or a thiazide diuretic.

If signs of shock (difficulty breathing, flushing of the whole body, angioedema, urticaria, an asthma attack and the like), thrombocytopenia, granulocytopenia, haemolytic anaemia, methaemoglobinaemia, reduced platelet function (prolonged bleeding time), cyanosis, nausea, vomiting, loss of appetite, gastrointestinal bleeding, peptic ulcer, perforation, hypersensitivity symptoms (facial swelling, sweating, low blood pressure), rash, Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), abnormal liver function such as raised AST or raised ALT, or fixed drug eruption occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.title: Soft Capsule (E58200ACS)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the supply of vitamins A, B1 and B2 in physical tiredness, during pregnancy and breast-feeding, when strength is reduced during or after illness, and in old age, and for the relief of dryness of the eyes, night blindness, angular cheilitis, cheilitis, stomatitis, glossitis, eczema, dermatitis, beriberi and eye strain.
groups.usage: Adults and those aged 8 years and older: take 2 capsules per dose, 2 times in 1 day.
groups.caution:
If a pregnant woman takes 5,000 IU or more of vitamin A in 1 day, it may cause birth defects. Women within the first 3 months of pregnancy and women who may be pregnant must not take it.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if the user is a baby under 3 months of age; if you have or have had hypersensitivity or an allergic reaction to soybean oil; or if you have hypersensitivity to soybean or peanut.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if the user is a baby under 1 year of age; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; if the user is a premature baby or a young child; if you have a disorder of fat metabolism such as hyperlipoproteinaemia, diabetic hyperlipidaemia or pancreatitis, or lipid emulsions must be given to you with caution; or if you have fat overload.

If symptoms do not improve after about 1 month of use, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist. Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. When it is given to a child, use it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian. The vitamin A in this medicine is supplied sufficiently by a normal diet, so the supplementary dose must not exceed 5,000 IU in 1 day. It may turn the urine yellow and so affect clinical test values. If you have a tendency to thrombosis such as blocked blood vessels, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

Consult a pharmacist if you take it together with an oral contraceptive containing oestrogen or an intravenous lipid preparation.

If nausea, vomiting, itching, dry and rough skin, painful swelling of the joints, loose stools, constipation, diarrhoea, loss of appetite, red spots, urticaria, eczema, rash, maculopapular rash, itching, oedema, or oedema or fluid retention in people with kidney failure or heart failure occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.usage: Adults and those aged 15 years and older: take 2 capsules per dose, 3 times in 1 day, 30 minutes after meals.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day, consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause liver damage.

If a severe skin adverse reaction such as acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis occurs, stop taking it and consult a pharmacist.

Do not take this medicine if you have or have had hypersensitivity to it; if you have had asthma after taking another antipyretic analgesic or a cold medicine; if the user is a baby under 3 months of age; or if you have severe or uncontrolled high blood pressure.

groups.title: Tablet (136601ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the relief of mild to moderate pain such as muscle pain, neuralgia, pain after injury and after surgery, headache, toothache and earache.
groups.usage: Adults: take 1 to 2 tablets (125 to 250 mg) per dose, 3 times in 1 day.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day, consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause gastrointestinal bleeding.

Taking this medicine increases the risk of serious and possibly fatal cardiovascular thrombotic events, myocardial infarction and stroke, and serious gastrointestinal adverse reactions such as gastrointestinal bleeding, ulceration and perforation may occur.

Do not take this medicine if you have peptic ulcer; if a medicine has caused problems in your stomach or duodenum; if you have hypersensitivity to it; if you have had asthma, urticaria or an allergic reaction to aspirin or another non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesic (including COX-2 inhibitors); if it is for the treatment of pain occurring before or after coronary artery bypass graft surgery (CABG); if you are pregnant or may be pregnant; if you have severe liver impairment, severe kidney impairment or severe heart failure; or if you have inflammatory bowel disease such as Crohn's disease or ulcerative colitis.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have had peptic ulcer; if the user is a child or you are an older person; if you have high blood pressure, fluid retention or heart failure; if you have bronchial asthma; or if you have or have had liver impairment or kidney impairment.

While you are taking this medicine, do not take it together with another non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesic, an ACE inhibitor or angiotensin II receptor antagonist, aspirin, a diuretic, lithium, methotrexate, a coumarin anticoagulant (warfarin and the like), ciclosporin or tacrolimus, an antiplatelet medicine, a selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor (SSRI) or a corticosteroid. Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you are also being treated for peptic ulcer with misoprostol or the like.

If nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, constipation, abdominal pain, gastrointestinal bleeding, peptic ulcer and perforation, or, rarely, shock, rash, itching, anaemia, raised AST and ALT, drowsiness, headache, dizziness, cold sweat, chills or an abnormal feeling of euphoria occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.title: Tablet (260300ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the relief of sneezing, runny nose, blocked nose and watering eyes caused by a nasal cold and by allergic and vasomotor rhinitis.
groups.usage: Adults: take 1 tablet per dose. Children aged 12 years to 14 years: take 1/2 tablet per dose. Take it 3 times in 1 day, after meals.
groups.caution:
If a severe skin adverse reaction such as acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis occurs, stop taking it and consult a pharmacist.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if you have severe liver or kidney impairment; if you have severe coronary heart disease; if you have difficulty passing urine with residual urine; if you have high blood pressure or coronary artery disease; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; if the user is a baby aged 2 years or younger; if you are being given an MAO inhibitor; if you have hypersensitivity to methyl parahydroxybenzoate; or if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Take care when driving or operating machinery after taking it.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have asthma, glaucoma, heart disease or arrhythmia, diabetes, an overactive thyroid or difficulty passing urine due to prostatic hyperplasia, or if the user is a child under 12 years of age.

If symptoms do not improve within 7 days, or if a high fever occurs at the same time, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

Do not take it together with a blood-pressure-lowering medicine, alcohol, a central nervous system depressant (hypnotic, sedative, tranquilliser), an MAO inhibitor, a sympathomimetic, a tricyclic antidepressant, guanethidine, bretylium, bethanidine, debrisoquine, methyldopa, a sympathomimetic medicine (decongestant, appetite suppressant, amphetamine-type stimulant) or an adrenergic blocker. Take this medicine at least 15 days after stopping an MAO inhibitor.

If central nervous system effects such as sedation, drowsiness, central nervous system depression, central stimulation, anxiety, sweating, a mild fall in blood pressure, visual disturbance, dilated pupils, delirium, hallucination, excitement, muscle cramps, stiffness, athetosis, clonic and tonic convulsions, high fever, respiratory paralysis, coma or circulatory paralysis occur, or if skin reactions, temporary stinging pain, a burning sensation, digestive effects such as thirst, nausea or vomiting, difficulty passing urine, excitement in a child, acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis, a severe skin adverse reaction such as fever, erythema or many small pustules, symptoms of ischaemic colitis such as sudden abdominal pain or rectal bleeding in connection with pseudoephedrine, or symptoms of posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome and reversible cerebral vasoconstriction syndrome such as sudden severe headache, thunderclap headache, nausea, vomiting, confusion, seizure or visual disturbance occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.usage: Adults: on the first day take 2 tablets per dose, 4 times in 1 day; after that, as a maintenance dose, take 1 tablet per dose, 4 times in 1 day. If rash, reddening of the skin, diarrhoea or constipation occurs, or occasionally loss of appetite, abdominal discomfort, nausea or vomiting, or rarely a tendency to bleed such as nosebleed or blood in the sputum occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.
